g.text: Time, motion and direction—a smart wearable system built around the idea that a rider’s
attention is more scarce than screen space.
The project framed navigation as a focused wearable experience. Instead of
reproducing a phone screen, eNav shows only the information needed in
ESP-32 DevKit V1 became the working board after exploring both ESP and
Raspberry Pi systems. The display and wiring were assembled into an early
Code was run through Arduino IDE to understand how each instruction
affected the board and display. Mock outputs were checked through the serial
After studying how PCB layers route overlapping and direct connections, a
custom circuit was laid out and hand-built on a DIY soldering board.
The custom board compressed the loose wiring into a compact plug-and-play
connection for the ESP-32 and display.
A complete Google Navigation view would require the Navigation API
embedded in the app. Mock code validated the information path before that
A third-party phone application supplied live navigation data to the ESP-32,
establishing the connected system from smartphone to focused wearable
The final direction packages the electronics as a compact, glanceable object
that reduces visual clutter and keeps the rider present on the road.
